sources: The day (NZ v IND, 2nd Test, Hagley Oval, Christchurch, 27 November 2026): the channel owner's ESPNcricinfo ball-by-ball capture of match 1539443 (517 deliveries: line, length, shot, control, wagon zone; the day's commentary text for speeds, chances and reviews). Every bowler's figures and every batter's runs reproduce the scorecard.

The edges: the five outside-edge fours (27.3 Latham, 44.2 Blundell, 58.6 and 61.5 Mitchell, 73.4 Phillips) are the balls Cricinfo flags 'not in control' that went for four past or through the slips; the commentary at 58.6 ('only two slips') and 61.5 ('no third slip') says the cordon was two slips. Cricinfo's scoring has Latham on strike for the catch dropped at 14.1 while its text names Conway: the video does not name the batter. Photographs supplied by the channel owner; Gurnoor Brar's debut and Dhruv Jurel's catch identified by the owner.

Ground history: Cricsheet men's Tests at Hagley Oval, 2014 to 2025 (cricsheet.org, ODC-BY): 15 Tests in our archive (partial coverage): first innings after 85 overs, scoring rate. Test 1 Day 1 (Basin Reserve, NZ 243/5): the channel's earlier Cricbuzz match capture. Analysis: analysis/nz2_day1.py, analysis/nz2_ground.py.
The cordon figure and the pitch map are our own illustrations: fielder positions are typical, not the actual field.

short.vo: Five times, New Zealand edged it past India's slips for four. Twenty runs. And twice, the commentators said the same thing: there is no third slip.

tiles.l: OUTSIDE EDGES FOR FOUR, THROUGH OR PAST THE SLIPS
TIMES THE COMMENTARY NOTED NO THIRD SLIP

short.vo: But first, a debut. गुरनूर बराड़ got his cap, and nineteen overs: four maidens, fifty-two runs. His first Test wicket came on the last ball before lunch: Conway, lbw, and the review confirmed it. Seven no-balls came with it.

scene.title: The debut.
scene.name: GURNOOR BRAR
scene.caption: First Test wicket: Conway lbw, last ball before lunch

short.vo: India chose to field. New Zealand finished two forty-six for five, off eighty-five overs, fifteen per cent slower than Hagley's usual.

scene.name: NEW ZEALAND
scene.caption: India chose to field. Hagley's usual: 3.39

short.vo: India's good-length balls went for one point four seven an over, and took four of the five wickets. Their full balls went for four point six one, and took none. Three times the price.

head.t: THE PRICE OF A FULL BALL
head.sub: RUNS PER OVER BY LENGTH · INDIA'S BOWLERS, DAY 1

short.vo: Between the forty-first and forty-fourth overs, three wickets fell for no runs. आकाश दीप took two, with the same ball: good length, close to off, seaming away.
Same ball, twice. Almost the same spot.

scene.footnote: AKASH DEEP BOTH TIMES · LINE AND LENGTH AS RECORDED

short.vo: Now look where the edges went. A keeper. Two slips. And a third slip who, on the day, was an empty chair. Five edges, through or past the cordon.

head.sub: WHERE THE FIVE EDGES WENT · ILLUSTRATIVE

scene.foot: POSITIONS ARE TYPICAL, NOT THE ACTUAL FIELD · EDGE DIRECTIONS FROM THE DAY'S WAGON DATA

short.vo: Twenty runs, eight per cent of the day. In fairness, a third slip means one fewer fielder somewhere else, and we can't see the plan.

tiles.l: RUNS FROM THE FIVE EDGES / THE DAY'S TOTAL
FALSE SHOTS THAT BECAME A WICKET

short.vo: India set one trap, and it worked. वॉशिंगटन सुंदर: drift, dip, a backward short leg waiting. Daryl Mitchell had worked five of his ten balls from him to midwicket or leg.

items.d: Sundar tossed it up, full, outside off
a catcher set for the back-foot clip
Mitchell worked half his balls from Sundar that way

short.vo: Then one turned and bounced. ध्रुव जुरेल, at backward short leg, dived and took it. A fielder in that spot, a bowler who dips it, a batter who goes back: that is a plan, and it worked.

scene.title: Taken.
scene.name: DHRUV JUREL
scene.caption: Turn, bounce, and a fielder waiting: the trap worked

short.vo: The catch that went down was at second slip, in the fourteenth over. India reviewed once and lost it. New Zealand reviewed twice, and one stuck.
At Hagley, first innings after eighty-five overs have read two thirty-two to four thirty-nine. New Zealand's two forty-six for five is the second slowest of seven.

head.sub: FIRST-INNINGS SCORE · MEN'S TESTS IN OUR ARCHIVE

short.vo: Same score as Wellington, two forty-three for five, but there all five wickets fell inside twenty-nine overs. Tomorrow, Blundell and Phillips resume, sixty-two unbroken, with a new ball behind them.

short.vo: India bowled well enough to win the day. The empty chair, and the full ball, had other ideas.

short.vo: Should India add a third slip? Comment one, yes. Two, no. Three, it's the full ball.

short.description:
India vs New Zealand, 2nd Test at Hagley Oval, Day 1 analysis: five outside edges for four past or through the slips (20 runs, 8% of New Zealand's 246 for 5), the empty third slip, Gurnoor Brar's debut (19-4-52-1, first Test wicket Conway lbw), the Washington Sundar and Dhruv Jurel backward-short-leg trap that dismissed Daryl Mitchell, the three wickets for no runs in overs 41 to 44, and why India's full balls cost 4.61 an over against 1.47 for good length. Hagley Oval history: after 85 overs of a first innings, New Zealand's 246 for 5 is the second slowest of seven in our archive. Comment 1 yes, 2 no, 3 the full ball: should India add a third slip?
